subject: System failure insight brief & recovery actions
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jorge Alvarez <jorge.alvarez@oakfieldpay.com>, Ava Rodgers <ava.rodgers@oakfieldpay.com>
Cc: Oakfield Payments Support <support@oakfieldpay.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: System failure — concise technical readout & next steps

Hi Jorge / Ava,

Thank you for the call this morning. As promised, attached is a concise customer-facing summary that explains what we found, the immediate mitigations we executed, and our next action items with owners and target dates. High level: a combination of an unexpected KV-cache eviction pattern and a degraded fallback path caused increased backend coordinator latency, which in turn produced sustained token-generation timeouts for requests routed to your dedicated pool between 06:12–06:47 PST on 2026-11-07.

What we are sharing in this thread: 1) a short RCA document (attached) with an annotated timeline; 2) the action ledger (owners + ETA) for remediation and verification; 3) a pointer to logs for your audit team.

Immediate mitigations (already applied):
- Temporarily increased KV-cache capacity for your dedicated pool to stop eviction cascades (completed 06:25 PST).
- Enabled a prioritized routing policy that routed in-flight requests to a warmed, compatible model variant for 13 minutes to avoid further timeouts.
- Rebalanced fetch backpressure knobs to prevent the coordinator from stalling under burst.

Planned next steps (owners stamped in the attached):
- Rafael: submit a durable fix to the cache eviction policy and add an auto-threshold guard (ETA: 2026-11-12).
- Hannah: run a verification sweep in a mirrored staging environment and deliver a verification report (ETA: 2026-11-09).
- Kimberly: coordinate a short verification window with your SREs next week and share the evidence bundle.

I recognize the impact this had on your environment and the disruption to customer flows. Our team is committed to both correcting the root cause and improving our cross-account detection/alerts so future incidents like this are prevented.

Attachments: Oakfield_Root_Cause_Summary_20261107.pdf (pdf) — one-page customer-facing RCA; kv-cache-timeline-logs-20261107.zip (log bundle, redwood internal logs masked where necessary).

If it helps, I can do a 30-minute technical walkthrough with your SREs tomorrow morning to step through the timeline and log excerpts. Please let me know a preferred time.

– Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the summary — I appreciate the clarity. Two quick asks from our side before the walkthrough: 1) can you confirm whether any customer data was exposed or replayed during the window; 2) for the verification sweep, can we get a checklist of the exact inputs you will replay so our compliance team can be present?

We would prefer a walkthrough at 08:00 PST tomorrow if that works for your team.

Regards,

Subject: Re: System failure — concise technical readout & next steps

Hi Jorge — answering inline and including the verification plan below. Rafael and Hannah are looped for technical detail and execution.

1) Data exposure: our initial forensics show no unauthorized data exfiltration and no request replay beyond the normal retry behavior. All affected requests returned 5xx timeouts rather than successful but duplicated responses. We are continuing a focused audit and will hand over the evidence bundle (redacted where required) to your compliance team.

2) Verification checklist (what we will replay/test in staging):
- Controlled KV-cache pressure test using Oakfield-like key distribution (log excerpts in the attached zip).
- Warm/cold model variant switching under rate (traffic ramp from 0–x rps to replicate peak).
- Coordinator backpressure test validating that the rebalancing knobs prevent stall at 2x typical peak.

Rough schedule for verification window (proposed):
- Monday 2026-11-09 08:00–09:30 PST: run replay with Oakfield SREs on call, capture latency and eviction metrics.
- Monday 2026-11-09 09:30–10:00 PST: review logs and preliminary verification report.

Owners and immediate action ledger (concise):
- Rafael Mendes (Engineering): apply eviction-policy guard, instrument additional metrics, PR for review by 2026-11-12.
- Hannah Schmitt (Operations): run the mirrored staging verification and produce the verification report by 2026-11-09.
- Kimberly Park (CS): schedule and run verification call with Oakfield, circulate evidence bundle, and coordinate a short follow-up on 2026-11-10 for acceptance.

Rafael: I've asked for a short annex with the code change outline and the risk notes — can you confirm the estimated rollout plan and whether there are any infra migrations tied to the change?

Thanks — we will share the Drive link to the evidence bundle before the Monday window.

– Kimberly

Kimberly / Jorge / team,

Following the verification window earlier today I wanted to confirm the concrete outcomes and next technical milestones:

What we ran (summary):
- Replayed key distribution and induced eviction under controlled load — observed the same eviction cascade pattern when cache pressure exceeded the previous guard threshold.
- Deployed a temporary guard that prevents concurrent eviction churn; after the change, coordinator latency remained within SLA for three successive ramp tests.

Verification results (short):
- Evidence: attached log excerpts and the verification report in the Drive link show no request duplication and no data exposure.
- Acceptance criteria met for the short-term guard: coordinator  p95 latency < 250ms for the recreated traffic profile.

Next technical milestones (owners / ETA):
- Rafael: submit the eviction-policy patch and accompanying unit/integration tests (PR to staging by 2026-11-12).
- Rafael & Hannah: staged rollout to dedicated pools with 24-hour monitoring and automated rollback trigger (start 2026-11-13).
- Kimberly: schedule a 30-minute acceptance call with Oakfield SREs on 2026-11-10 14:00 PST to confirm the report and close the loop.

Jorge / Ava — thank you for joining the verification session. If you're comfortable with the results, we'll proceed to the staged rollout and send a short email update when the change hits production for your pools.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
